text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, keep endpoints simple and predictable, and use nouns in URLs, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Clear documentation is essential, because developers need to know how each endpoint works without guessing. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that old clients keep working when you make changes. Following these practices saves time and reduces frustration for everyone.
